verses.text: These are the family leaders and the people listed with them who went up with me from Babylon while King Artaxerxes ruled:
From the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom. From the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel. From the descendants of David, Hattush.
From the descendants of Shecaniah, from the descendants of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him one hundred fifty men listed in the family records.
From the descendants of Pahath-Moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men.
From the descendants of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred men.
From the descendants of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men.
From the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men.
From the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty men.
From the descendants of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred eighteen men.
From the descendants of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred sixty men.
From the descendants of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men.
From the descendants of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred ten men.
From the descendants of Adonikam, who came later: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men.
From the descendants of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud, and with them seventy men.
I gathered them together at the river that flows toward Ahava, and we camped there for three days. When I looked over the people and the priests, I found that there were no Levites there.
So I sent for these leaders: Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. I also sent for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were teachers.

I sent them to Iddo, the leader at the place called Casiphia. I told them what to say to Iddo and his relatives, the temple servants at Casiphia, so they would send us servants for the temple of our God.
Because our God's kind hand was on us, they brought us a wise man named Sherebiah, from the descendants of Mahli, son of Levi, son of Israel. He came with his sons and relatives, eighteen men.
They also brought Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah from the descendants of Merari, with his relatives and their sons, twenty men.
They also brought two hundred twenty of the temple servants, a group David and his officials had set up to help the Levites. All of them were listed by name.
There by the Ahava River, I announced that we would go without food and humble ourselves before our God. We asked him for a safe journey for us, our children, and everything we owned.

I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the road. We had told the king, "Our God's kind hand is on everyone who looks to him, but his power and anger are against everyone who leaves him."
So we went without food and prayed to our God about this, and he answered our prayer.
Then I chose twelve of the leading priests, along with Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their relatives.
I weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the objects that the king, his advisers, his officials, and all the Israelites there had given for the temple of our God.
I weighed out to them about twenty-two tonnes of silver, silver objects weighing about three and a half tonnes, about three and a half tonnes of gold,
twenty gold bowls weighing about eight and a half kilograms, and two fine objects of polished bronze, as valuable as gold.
I said to them, "You are holy to the LORD, and these objects are holy. The silver and gold are a gift freely given to the LORD, the God of your ancestors.
Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in the rooms of the LORD's temple in Jerusalem, in front of the leading priests, the Levites, and the family leaders of Israel."
So the priests and Levites took the silver, gold, and objects that had been weighed out, to bring them to the temple of our God in Jerusalem.
On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River to go to Jerusalem. Our God's hand was on us, and he protected us from enemies and robbers along the way.
We arrived in Jerusalem and rested there for three days.

On the fourth day, in the temple of our God, we weighed out the silver, gold, and objects and gave them to Meremoth son of Uriah the priest. Eleazar son of Phinehas was with him, and so were the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
Everything was counted and weighed, and the total weight was written down at that time.

Then the people who had come back from being prisoners offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.
They also gave the king's orders to the king's officers and to the governors west of the Euphrates River. Then these officials helped the people and the temple of God.
